title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models
claim: A single-prompt linear path crosses a trade-off, whereas two decoupled endpoints joined by a corridor stay in the low-loss valley.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right (before, during, after), shared loss heatmap, accuracy insets, bottom legend
description: Three heatmap panels show a joint cross-entropy loss landscape in CLIP text-feature space. Dark blue marks low loss and red marks high loss. The left panel, 'Before DMC', shows a nearly straight grey single-prompt path between a green baseline point and an orange zero-shot point. Its inset plots base accuracy (orange), novel accuracy (pink) and harmonic mean (dashed grey) against alpha, and base and novel cross over. The middle panel, 'During DMC training', is a 2x2 grid of epochs 0, 5, 50 and 100. A blue generalization circle separates from a pink specialization square. The right panel, 'After DMC training', shows a curved blue corridor through the blue valley, with a star at the operating point alpha=0.2. Its inset shows base and novel accuracy both high and stable. A colorbar sits on the right and a legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Decoupled Mode Connectivity on Flowers102 (joint CE loss landscape). The 2D plane in CLIP text-feature space is anchored at fw1 (zero-shot CLIP); the x-axis spans toward f ˆ w2 (fine-tuned CoOp checkpoint) and the y-axis is the Gram–Schmidt orthogonal component of fgen (text features of DMC’s converged generalization prompt) relative to fw1. Each grid point is re-normalized per class before the joint base+novel CE loss is evaluated; construction details in Appendix G. Before DMC (left): the single-prompt baseline traces the linear path; the inset shows the base–novel trade-off, with base and novel accuracies crossing over as α varies. During DMC (middle): the two prompts start collapsed at f ˆ w2 (epoch 0) and separate during training. After DMC (right): the converged DMC corridor lies inside the low-loss valley, with the operating point at α = 0.20 marked by the star; the inset confirms base and novel accuracies are both high and stable along the corridor.
abstract: Prompt learning adapts vision-language models such as CLIP by optimizing a short learnable prompt. The cross-entropy objective pulls this prompt toward base-class specialization, whereas generalization to unseen classes benefits from staying close to CLIP's zero-shot feature space. Because both objectives act on the same prompt, their gradients conflict at convergence, and in our experiments no single-prompt loss design clearly improves on the cosine baseline. We propose Decoupled Mode Connectivity (DMC), which gives each objective its own prompt. Starting from a base-trained prompt, DMC trains a specialization prompt and a generalization prompt, and merges their text features with a fixed coefficient at test time, at the inference cost of a single prompt. A linear mode connectivity (LMC) corridor in text-feature space keeps the classification loss low for every classifier interpolated between the two endpoints, and a Visual Anchor KL term preserves CLIP's zero-shot class-similarity distribution of each image during specialization. We further argue that such regularizers should satisfy class-permutation invariance (CPI), and show via Fano's inequality, in an idealized model, that violating CPI lower-bounds the drop in novel accuracy by a term proportional to the mutual information between the prompt and the base-class labels. Across 11 datasets, DMC improves the average harmonic mean of base and novel accuracy over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp, and its interpolation curves pass beyond the single-prompt operating point, shifting the base-novel frontier rather than trading along it. Code is available at https://github.com/IemProg/DMC.
